ticket_claim_110.note: The 110 was exact on 2026-10-20 and is stale. On this tree there are 129 classes named *Rule or *Rules, one of which (ScanRule) is the shared engine rather than a guard, so 128 guards carry that name -- and 32 more guards do not follow the convention at all (FullLayerMatrixTests, ResultFailureConversionTests, MaybeAbsenceTests, TokenTrackingRatchet, FatInterfaceShapeRatchet and the other *Tests-named guards). The real population is 160.

tiers.A: catches a defect and is cheap: the verdict is derived from the product's structure, and an innocent change (a rename, a move, a new type) does not require editing the rule. false_positive_cost 0.
tiers.B: catches a defect but is noisy: an innocent change forces a manual edit of the rule or of one of its ledgers. false_positive_cost 1 or 2.
tiers.C: does not catch a defect: it fires on the tree's shape (a measurement, a pinned count, a renamed declaration), or it no longer decides anything.

cost_legend.0: never: the rule re-derives everything it grades.
cost_legend.1: rarely: one manual edit of the rule or of one ledger row per relevant change.
cost_legend.2: often: the rule carries a written-down number, a name list or a path table that every relevant change moves.

kind_legend.roslyn-analyzer: the rule grades source TEXT today; a Roslyn analyzer over the product tree decides the same question by TYPE. This is the #1729 pilot shape.
kind_legend.derived-value: the rule's instrument is bound to form: it compares a live measurement with a written-down number or list. The repair is to DERIVE the value, so the check survives the change.
kind_legend.il-probe: the rule already decides by symbol (reflection over the loaded assembly, or Mono.Cecil over the IL). No conversion needed -- it is the shape the others should move to.

rules.defect_signal: ProjectionCache declared six members non-nullable and initialised them with null!, so the compiler was asked to accept a value nobody assigned.
rules.refactor_signal: The nine assembly paths are named; a rename of an assembly needs an edit.
evidence: measured: no firing in the window

rules.subject: A singleton's own documentation and its DI registration must agree about thread safety.
rules.checks: Reads the projector's registration lifetime and its own doc comment and asserts the two agree.
rules.defect_signal: #605: DefaultUiProjector documented itself as NOT thread-safe while the only shipped DI host registered it, and its only consumer, as singletons -- so the consequence was a crash rather than a stale frame.
rules.refactor_signal: The scope is a single type, read from the assembly.
evidence: measured: no firing in the window

rules.subject: A Result is read through Match, not through .Value.
rules.checks: Source-scans for `.Value` on a Result and grades each site; since #1868 a type-resolving analyzer (HARCH00x) decides the same question by type, and the text rule is the differential oracle.
rules.defect_signal: #602: two call sites read (await _configStore.LoadAsync()).Value, and Result<T>.Value on a failure throws ResultFailureException -- so `harbor ask` died with an unhandled exception on a hand-edited config.json.
rules.refactor_signal: The scope is a tree scan; the exemption list is short.
evidence: run 39414753478 (arch/1868-result-read-analyzer): the analyzer saw a site the text rule did not -- defect

rules.subject: HARCH003's own tests: the planted controls, the gate over the live tree, and the differential against the pattern matcher it replaces.
rules.checks: Runs the Roslyn analyzer in-process over planted offenders, over the live tree, and against AvaloniaFireAndForgetRules' spelling matcher.
rules.defect_signal: An unobserved Task (the #948 class: async void swallows everything after await) reaches the product with nobody noticing.
rules.refactor_signal: The differential against the retired matcher is expected to drift: the matcher asks about the SPELLING, the analyzer about the TYPE, and the disagreement in both directions is the point.
evidence: commit f29ce361 'the lost observations are fixed and the fire-and-forget rule decides by type'

rules.subject: The vendored HTML helpers must not be a second implementation of one behaviour.
rules.checks: Compares the two vendored CollapseWhitespace implementations against each other by re-typing both and comparing over an exhaustive alphabet.
rules.defect_signal: #878: the two vendored helpers disagree on 758 of the whitespace cases, so a behaviour that looked like one thing was two.
rules.refactor_signal: The rule grades the VENDORED tree, which is not built by CI: a change there is not caught by the compiler, which is the point.
evidence: measured: no firing in the window

rules.subject: The catalog name and the registered name of a tool are the same name.
rules.checks: Reads the [ToolInfo] attributes of the builtin tools and compares each with the catalog's entry for that tool.
rules.defect_signal: #1564 moved 292 tool-name literals into one catalog; two places still had to keep a literal (an attribute argument and a case label), and if the two disagree the permission and the registration disagree.
rules.refactor_signal: The names are read from the assembly; the tool set is derived.
evidence: measured: no firing in the window
